zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿لا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْها ولا يُنْـزِفُونَ﴾ — its interpretation is: from drinking it they are not afflicted by the headache (ṣudāʿ) that afflicts the people of this world. ﴿وَلا يُنْـزِفُونَ﴾: they do not become intoxicated. "اَلنَّزِيفُ" is the drunk man; he is called "نَزِيفٌ" and "مَنزُوفٌ" only because his reason has been drained away (nazafa). It is also read: "وَلا يُنْزَفُونَ", meaning: their drink does not run out.

zajjaj:22-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحُورٌ عِينٌ﴾ ﴿كَأمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ المَكْنُونِ﴾ — with the genitive (khafḍ); it has also been read with the nominative (rafʿ). Those who read it with the nominative disliked the genitive because it would be a conjunction (ʿaṭf) onto His saying: ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 17] ﴿بِأكْوابٍ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 18]; so they said: the ḥūr are not among the things that are carried round. But it is genitive on a basis other than what these people supposed, because the meaning of ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 17] is: they are blessed with this, and likewise they are blessed with the flesh of fowl, and likewise they are blessed with ḥūr ʿīn. Whoever read with the nominative has the better of the two options, because the meaning of ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 17] with these things is: that which has been established for them; so it is as if He said: "وَلَهم حُورٌ عِينٌ" (and they shall have ḥūr ʿīn). Similar to it, among what is construed according to the meaning (al-ḥaml ʿalā al-maʿnā), is the poet's saying:
بادَتْ وغُيِّرَ آيُهُنَّ مَعَ البِلى ∗∗∗ إلّا رَواكِدَ جَمْرُهُنَّ هَباءُ
(They have perished and their traces have been altered with decay, except the firm-set hearthstones whose embers are dust)
وَمُشَجَّجٌ أمّا سَواءُ قَذالُهُ ∗∗∗ فَبَدا وغَيَّرَ سارَهُ المِعْزاءُ
(and a battered tent-peg, whose head has become exposed, while the stony ground has altered the rest of it)
Because he said "إلّا رَواكِدَ", the meaning was: "بِها رَواكِدُ" (in it there are firm-set stones), so he construed "وَمُشَجَّجٌ" according to the meaning. It has also been read: "وَحُورًا عِينًا", with the accusative (naṣb), likewise by construal according to the meaning, because the meaning is: "they are given these things, they are given ḥūr ʿīn"; except that this reading differs from the Muṣḥaf, which is the Imām (the standard codex), and the people of knowledge dislike that anything be read which differs from the Imām. The meaning of "اَلْحُورُ" is: women of intense whiteness; and "اَلْعِينُ": women with large eyes, beautiful ones. The meaning of ﴿كَأمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ المَكْنُونِ﴾ is: like pearls when they come out of their shell and covering, unaltered by time and the changing conditions of use. By His saying ﴿كَأمْثالِ اللُّؤْلُؤِ﴾ He means only: in their purity and their lustre, like the purity and lustre of pearls.

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ — accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "that is done for them as a recompense for their deeds". It is also possible that "جَزاءً" be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 17] is: they are recompensed with a recompense for their deeds. This option is the one most grammarians hold.

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿إلا قِيلا سَلامًا سَلامًا﴾ — "قِيلًا" is accusative by His saying: "لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْوًا ولا تَأْثِيمًا، إلّا قِيلًا سَلامًا سَلامًا"; so the meaning is: "they hear nothing but a saying: سَلامًا سَلامًا". It is accusative on two counts. One of them is that it be a naʿt (adjective) of "قِيلًا", so that the meaning is: "they hear nothing but speech in which there is safety (yaslamu) from idle talk and sin". The second option is that ﴿سَلامًا﴾ be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), so that the meaning is: "they hear nothing in it except that some of them say to others: سَلامًا سَلامًا (peace, peace)". The evidence for this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿تَحِيَّتُهم فِيها سَلامٌ﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 23].

zajjaj:28-29.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِي سِدْرٍ مَخْضُودٍ﴾ ﴿وَطَلْحٍ مَنضُودٍ﴾ — "اَلْمَخْضُودُ" is that whose thorns have been stripped off. As for "اَلطَّلْحُ", it has come in the exegesis (tafsīr) that it is the banana tree. "اَلطَّلْحُ" is also the umm ghaylān tree (acacia), and it is possible that this tree is what is meant, because it has blossoms of a very fragrant scent; so they were addressed and promised the like of what they love, except that its superiority over what is in this world is like the superiority of everything else in Paradise over what is in this world.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ﴾ — its meaning is: complete and perpetual.

zajjaj:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿وَماءٍ مَسْكُوبٍ﴾ — what is meant is that it is water over which they take no toil; it pours out for them however they like.

zajjaj:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿إنّا أنْشَأْناهُنَّ إنْشاءً﴾ — He means the ḥūr: they were brought into being for the friends (awliyāʾ) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and are not among those who underwent birth.

zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُنَّ أبْكارًا﴾: they have not been touched.

zajjaj:37-37.t: ﴿عُرُبًا﴾ — "اَلْعُرُبُ" are those who show love to their husbands.

zajjaj:39-40.t: His saying: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ ﴿وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الآخِرِينَ﴾ — its meaning, and Allah knows best, is: "a company of those who followed the Prophet ﷺ and saw him with their own eyes, and a company of those who believed in him and came after him."

zajjaj:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿وَظِلٍّ مِن يَحْمُومٍ﴾ — "اَلْيَحْمُومُ" is that which is intensely black. It has been said that it is intensely black smoke; and it has been said that ﴿وَظِلٍّ مِن يَحْمُومٍ﴾ means: of a fire with which they are punished. The evidence for this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهم مِن فَوْقِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ مِنَ النّارِ ومِن تَحْتِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ﴾ [al-Zumar: 16]; except that here it is described as intensely black.

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿وَكانُوا يُصِرُّونَ عَلى الحِنْثِ العَظِيمِ﴾ — it has been said in the exegesis: "اَلْحِنْثُ" is shirk (associating partners with Allah); and it has been said: "upon the great sin". It is, and Allah knows best, shirk and disbelief in the resurrection, because in the Quran there is evidence of that, namely: ﴿وَأقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أيْمانِهِمْ لا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَن يَمُوتُ بَلى وعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا﴾ [al-Naḥl: 38]. So this, and Allah knows best, is their persistence in the great ḥinth.

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿فَشارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الهِيمِ﴾ — it is also read: "شَرْبَ الهِيمِ". "اَلشَّرْبُ" is the maṣdar (verbal noun) and "اَلشُّرْبُ" is the noun; it has also been said that al-shurb is likewise a maṣdar. "اَلْهِيمُ" are thirsty camels.

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿هَذا نُـزُلُهم يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾ — that is: this is their nourishment on the Day of Recompense, that is, the day they are recompensed for their deeds.

zajjaj:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿أفَرَأيْتُمْ ما تُمْنُونَ﴾ — that is: the semen (manī) that comes from you, from which the child comes into being. One says: "أمْنى الرَّجُلُ، يُمَنِي" and "مَنى، يَمْنِي"; so on this basis "تَمْنُونَ" with fatḥa on the tāʾ would be permissible, but I know of no one who read it so; so do not read it so unless a transmission is established.

zajjaj:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿أأنْتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُ أمْ نَحْنُ الخالِقُونَ﴾ — He argued against them concerning the resurrection by His power to originate creation, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنا مَثَلا ونَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ قالَ مَن يُحْيِي العِظامَ وهي رَمِيمٌ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 78] ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وهو بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 79].

zajjaj:60-61.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ المَوْتَ وما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ ﴿عَلى أنْ نُبَدِّلَ أمْثالَكم ونُنْشِئَكم في ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — that is: if We wished to create a creation other than you, no one would outstrip Us, nor would that escape Us.
His saying: ﴿وَنُنْشِئَكم في ما لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — that is: if We wished to make apes and swine out of you, We would not be outstripped, nor would that escape Us.

zajjaj:62-62.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ النَّشْأةَ الأُولى فَلَوْلا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ — that is: you have known the origination of creation, so why have you denied the resurrection? The meaning of "لَوْلا تَذَكَّرُونَ" is: will you not then remember (hallā tadhakkarūn)?

zajjaj:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾ — that is: if We made what you sow into debris (ḥuṭām), that is, rendered it void until it is broken to pieces, with no wheat in it nor anything of what you sow, ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾, that is: you would remain regretting. "فَظِلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ", with kasra on the ẓāʾ, is also permissible.

zajjaj:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿إنّا لَمُغْرَمُونَ﴾ — that is: they say: we have suffered loss and our crop is gone; ﴿بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 67].

zajjaj:69-69.t: His saying: ﴿أأنْتُمْ أنْـزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ المُزْنِ أمْ نَحْنُ المُنْـزِلُونَ﴾ — it (al-muzn) is the clouds; its singular is "مُزْنَةٌ" and its plural is "مُزْنٌ".

zajjaj:70-70.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْ نَشاءُ جَعَلْناهُ أُجاجًا﴾ — "اَلْأُجاجُ" is salt water that cannot possibly be drunk at all. ﴿فَلَوْلا تَشْكُرُونَ﴾: its meaning is "فَهَلّا" (will you not then).

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَرَأيْتُمُ النّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: you strike fire. You say: "وَرى الزَّنْدُ يَرِي، ورْيًا، فَهو وارٍ" when fire is struck from the fire-stick (zand), and "أوْرَيْتُ النّارَ" when you have struck it. The Arabs strike fire with the zand and the zanda, which are pieces of wood rubbed one against the other so that fire comes out of them. So He said: ﴿أأنْتُمْ أنْشَأْتُمْ شَجَرَتَها أمْ نَحْنُ المُنْشِئُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 72] ﴿نَحْنُ جَعَلْناها تَذْكِرَةً ومَتاعًا لِلْمُقْوِينَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 73], that is: when the beholder sees it he remembers Hell and the punishment he fears, and so he remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and seeks refuge with Him from it. As for the meaning of "مَتاعًا لِّلْمُقْوِينَ": "اَلْمُقْوِي" is the one who alights in al-qiwāʾ, which is empty land. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned everything that points to His oneness, and the favours He bestowed on them in creating them and nourishing them with what they eat and drink, which points to His power and His uniqueness; then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ العَظِيمِ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 74], that is: declare Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, free (of every imperfection).

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِمَواقِعِ النُّجُومِ﴾ — its meaning is "أُقْسِمُ" (I swear), and "لا" entered as tawkīd (emphasis), as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِئَلا يَعْلَمَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 29], whose meaning is: "that the People of the Book may know". The mawāqiʿ of the stars are the places where they set, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ المَشارِقِ والمَغارِبِ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 40]. It has also been said that by the mawāqiʿ of the stars (nujūm) is meant "the instalments (nujūm) of the Quran", because it used to be sent down upon the Prophet ﷺ in instalments, one thing after another; and the evidence for this view is: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 76] ﴿إنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 77].

zajjaj:78-78.t: His saying: ﴿فِي كِتابٍ مَكْنُونٍ﴾ — that is: guarded in heaven, in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).

zajjaj:79-79.t: His saying: ﴿لا يَمَسُّهُ إلا المُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ — by this are meant the angels: none touches it in the Preserved Tablet except the angels. It is also read: "اَلْمُطَهِّرُونَ", which is a rare reading, and it has two interpretations. One of them: "those who have purified themselves of sins"; the second is that it be "those who purify others".

zajjaj:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿تَنْـزِيلٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ — it is a ṣifa (adjective) of His saying "كَرِيمٌ"; and if you wish, it is nominative (marfūʿ) on the reading: "هُوَ تَنْزِيلٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ" (it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds).

zajjaj:81-81.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَبِهَذا الحَدِيثِ أنْتُمْ مُدْهِنُونَ﴾ — that is: "is it the Quran that you deny?" "اَلْمُدْهِنُ" is the one who temporises (al-mudāhin), and the lying hypocrite.

zajjaj:82-82.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكم أنَّكم تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ — they used to say: "we have been given rain by such-and-such a star (nawʾ)", and would not ascribe the watering to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. So it was said to them: do you make your provision — that is, your thanks for what you have been provided — denial? It has been read: "وَتَجْعَلُونَ شُكْرَكم أنَّكُمْ", but it ought not to be read so, because it differs from the Muṣḥaf. They have said that the interpretation of "رِزْقَكُمْ" here is thanks (al-shukr), and they have transmitted that one says "وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقِي" in the sense of "شُكْرِي" (my thanks); but this is not sound. Rather, the wording of His saying ﴿وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكم أنَّكم تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ points to the meaning "وَتَجْعَلُونَ شُكْرَكم أنَّكم تُكَذِّبُونَ", that is: you make the thanks for your provision that you say "we have been given rain by such-and-such a star", and so you lie in that.

zajjaj:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلا إذا بَلَغَتِ الحُلْقُومَ﴾ — He means: "when the soul (al-rūḥ) reaches the throat".

zajjaj:84-84.t: ﴿وَأنْتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ — that is: you, O family of the dying man, in that state see him having reached the point where his soul departs.

zajjaj:85-85.t: ﴿وَنَحْنُ أقْرَبُ إلَيْهِ مِنكم ولَكِنْ لا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that no one dies until he knows whether he is of the people of Paradise or of the people of the Fire.

zajjaj:87-87.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَرْجِعُونَها إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ — its meaning is: why do you not bring back the soul, if you are not "مَدِينِينَ", that is, not owned and governed, having no power over life and death? So why not, if you are as you claimed — like that saying of yours which has come in the Quran: ﴿الَّذِينَ قالُوا لإخْوانِهِمْ وقَعَدُوا لَوْ أطاعُونا ما قُتِلُوا قُلْ فادْرَءُوا عَنْ أنْفُسِكُمُ المَوْتَ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 168], as He said: ﴿أوْ كانُوا غُزًّى لَوْ كانُوا عِنْدَنا ما ماتُوا وما قُتِلُوا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 156]? So the meaning is: "if you are able to postpone an appointed term, why then do you not bring back the soul when it reaches the throat, and why do you not avert death from yourselves?"

zajjaj:88-89.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأمّا إنْ كانَ مِنَ المُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ ﴿فَرَوْحٌ ورَيْحانٌ﴾ — with fatḥa on the rāʾ in "رَوْحٌ"; its meaning is: then rest and coolness; and rayḥān is provision (rizq). The poet said:
سَلامُ الإلَهِ ورَيْحانُهُ ∗∗∗ ورَحْمَتُهُ وسَماءٌ دُرَرْ
(The peace of God and His provision (rayḥān), and His mercy, and a sky pouring abundant rain)
It has also been transmitted as "فَرُوحٌ", with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and its interpretation is: "then perpetual life with no death after it; and rayḥān is provision". It is also possible that "رَيْحانٌ" here be a greeting for the people of Paradise. The grammarians agree that the origin of "رَيْحانٌ" in the language is "رَيِّحانٌ", from the roots with wāw (dhawāt al-wāw); so the origin is "رَيْوِحانٌ": the wāw was changed to yāʾ and the first (yāʾ) was assimilated (udghimat) into it, so it became "رَيِّحانٌ"; then it was lightened, just as they said "مَيْتٌ" for "مَيِّتٌ". Doubling (tashdīd) is not permissible in "رَيْحانٌ" except as a far-fetched option, because alif and nūn have been added to it, so it was lightened by dropping the (second) yāʾ, and the lightening was made obligatory for it. Its nominative (rafʿ) is on the meaning: "as for him, if the deceased is of those brought near, then for him there is rawḥ and rayḥān".

zajjaj:90-91.t: His saying: ﴿وَأمّا إنْ كانَ مِن أصْحابِ اليَمِينِ﴾ ﴿فَسَلامٌ لَكَ مِن أصْحابِ اليَمِينِ﴾ — He has already made clear what belongs to the Companions of the Right at the beginning of the sūra. The meaning of ﴿فَسَلامٌ لَكَ مِن أصْحابِ اليَمِينِ﴾ is that you see in them the safety (salāma) you love, and you have already learned the recompense prepared for them.

zajjaj:92-93.t: His saying: ﴿وَأمّا إنْ كانَ مِنَ المُكَذِّبِينَ الضّالِّينَ﴾ ﴿فَنُـزُلٌ مِن حَمِيمٍ﴾ — it is read "فَنُزْلٌ", with the lightened form and with the heavy form. Its meaning is: "then nourishment of scalding water and roasting in Hellfire", that is: abiding in Hellfire. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that Hellfire here is for the deniers who go astray.

zajjaj:95-95.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَهو حَقُّ اليَقِينِ﴾ — that is: this which We have narrated to you in this sūra of accounts, and what Allah has prepared for His friends and His enemies, and what has been mentioned of what points to His oneness, is certainty, the truth of certainty; just as you say: "إنَّ زَيْدًا لَعالِمٌ حَقُّ عالِمٍ" (Zayd is a scholar, truly a scholar) and "إنَّهُ لَلْعالِمُ حَقُّ العالِمِ" (he is the scholar, truly the scholar), when you intensify the emphasis.

zajjaj:96-96.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ العَظِيمِ﴾ — that is: declare Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, free of evil, because the meaning of "سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ" is declaring Allah free of evil. Thus it has come from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and thus the lexicographers explain it: "the freedom (barāʾa) of Allah from evil". Sībawayh cited in this sense:
أقُولُ لِما جاءَ في فَخْرِهِ ∗∗∗ سُبْحانَ مِن عَلْقَمَةَ الفاجِرِ
(I say, when his boasting reached me: I am quit of ʿAlqama the wicked!)
That is: I declare myself quit of him.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إذا وقَعَتِ الواقِعَةُ﴾: of everything that comes which was being expected one says "qad waqaʿa" (it has occurred). You say "qad waqaʿa l-amru" (the matter has occurred), like your saying "qad jāʾa l-amru" (the matter has come). "اَلْواقِعَةُ" here is the Hour and the Resurrection.

zajjaj:10-11.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والسّابِقُونَ السّابِقُونَ﴾ ﴿أُولَئِكَ المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "The foremost, those foremost in the obedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and in affirming the truth of His prophets." The first "اَلسّابِقُونَ" is nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ, subject), the second is tawkīd (emphasis), and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿أُولَئِكَ المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾. Then He told where their abode is, saying: ﴿فِي جَنّاتِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 12]. And it may be that the first "اَلسّابِقُونَ" is nominative as the mubtadaʾ and its khabar is the second "اَلسّابِقُونَ", so that the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Those foremost in the obedience of Allah are the foremost to the mercy of Allah", and ﴿أُولَئِكَ المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾ would be part of their description.

zajjaj:13-14.t: And His saying: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مِنَ الآخِرِينَ﴾: "ثُلَّةٌ" is nominative in the sense of "They are a thulla"; "اَلثُّلَّةُ" is a group. This — and Allah knows best — is the meaning of ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾, that is: a group of those who saw the prophets with their own eyes and believed them; for those who saw all the prophets and believed them are more numerous than those who saw the Prophet, peace be upon him. That is His saying — in the story of Yūnus —: ﴿وَأرْسَلْناهُ إلى مِائَةِ ألْفٍ أوْ يَزِيدُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 147] ﴿فَآمَنُوا فَمَتَّعْناهم إلى حِينٍ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 148]: these are besides all the others who believed in all the prophets among those who saw them and believed them. And "اَلثُّلَّةُ" may be in the sense of "a few of the former and a few of the latter", because the derivation of al-thulla is from "the piece (al-qiṭʿa)": "al-thall" is breaking and cutting, and "al-thulla" is like a party (fiʾa) or a faction (firqa).

zajjaj:15-16.t:
And His saying: ﴿عَلى سُرُرٍ مَوْضُونَةٍ﴾ ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْها مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾: "مُتَّكِئِينَ" and "مُتَقابِلِينَ" are both accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "Those are the ones brought near, in the gardens of bliss, in this state." "اَلسُّرُرُ" is the plural of "سَرِيرٌ" (couch), like "كَثِيبٌ" and "كُثُبٌ". The meaning of "مُتَقابِلِينَ" is: they look at one another's faces, and look at the backs of one another's heads «[Translator's note: so in the source (ويَنْظُرُ في أقْفاءِ بَعْضٍ); the sense presumably intended is "and do not look at the backs of one another's heads".]». They are described, along with their bliss, by good companionship, refined character and purity of affection. Of this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَـزَعْنا ما في صُدُورِهِمْ مِن غِلٍّ إخْوانًا عَلى سُرُرٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 47]. It has come in the exegesis that "مَوْضُونَةٍ" means marmūla, and the meaning of "مَرْمُولَةٌ" is: woven, like the weaving of coats of mail; and it has come in the exegesis that they are of gold. An example of "مَوْضُونَةٌ" is the saying of al-Aʿshā:
؎وَمِن نَسْجِ داوُدَ مَوْضُونَةٌ ∗∗∗ يُساقُ بِها الحَيُّ عِيرًا فَعِيرا
(And close-woven [mail] of David's weaving, which the tribe carries along, caravan after caravan.)

zajjaj:17-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ ﴿بِأكْوابٍ وأبارِيقَ﴾: "اَلْأكْوابُ" are vessels that have no handles and no spouts, and "اَلْإبْرِيقُ" is what has a spout and a handle. ﴿وَكَأْسٍ مِن مَعِينٍ﴾: "اَلْكَأْسُ" is the vessel with drink in it; if there is no drink in it, it is not a kaʾs.
And His saying: ﴿مِن مَعِينٍ﴾: its meaning is: of wine flowing from springs.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِها كاذِبَةٌ﴾, that is: nothing repels it, as you say "qad ḥamala fulānun lā yukadhdhibu" (So-and-so charged without flinching), that is: nothing repels his charge. "كاذِبَةٌ" is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like your saying "ʿāfāhu llāhu ʿāfiyatan" (Allah granted him well-being) and "ʿāqabahu ʿāqibatan" (He punished him); and likewise "kadhdhaba kādhibatan". These are nouns standing in the position of maṣdars.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ﴾: the meaning is that it lowers the people of sin and raises the people of obedience. As for ﴿خافِضَةٌ رافِعَةٌ﴾, the reading is with the nominative; the accusative is permissible, but no imam among the Readers read it so, though it has been transmitted from al-Yazīdī «[Translator's note: the source has الزيدي, "al-Zaydī"; the companion of Abū ʿAmr is known as al-Yazīdī.]», the companion of Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ. Whoever reads the nominative — and that is the proper way — the meaning is: "It is lowering, raising." And whoever reads the accusative does so in one of two ways. One of them is: "When the Event occurs, lowering, raising", as a ḥāl (circumstantial). And it may be with "تَقَعُ" implied, the meaning being: "When it occurs, it occurs lowering, raising", as a ḥāl from the implied "تَقَعُ".

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿إذا رُجَّتِ الأرْضُ رَجًّا﴾: the position of "إذا" is accusative; the meaning is: "When it occurs at that time." The accusative may also be on the basis of "it occurs when the earth is shaken with a shaking". The meaning of ﴿رُجَّتِ﴾ is: it is moved with violent motion and quaked.

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿وَبُسَّتِ الجِبالُ بَسًّا﴾: "بُسَّتْ" means: moistened and mixed; and "بُسَّتْ" also means: driven along.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
﴿فَكانَتْ هَباءً مُنْبَثًّا﴾: dust. Similar to it is ﴿وَسُيِّرَتِ الجِبالُ فَكانَتْ سَرابًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 20]. An example of "mixed and moistened" is the poet's saying:
؎لا تَخْبِزا خَبْزًا وبُسّا بَسّا
(Do not bake bread, you two, but mix [the flour] a mixing.)
And an example of "driven and moving along" is his saying:
؎وانْبَسَّ حَيّاتُ الكَثِيبِ الأهْيَلِ
(And the snakes of the shifting sand-dune crept along.)

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ أزْواجًا ثَلاثَةً﴾, that is: three kinds. Kinds that go together with one another are called "أزْواجٌ", just as a pair of khuffs (leather socks) is called "zawjān".

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿فَأصْحابُ المَيْمَنَةِ ما أصْحابُ المَيْمَنَةِ﴾ is nominative by ibtidāʾ (as mubtadaʾ, subject); the meaning is: "And the companions of the right — what are they?! What sort of thing are they?! ﴿وَأصْحابُ المَشْأمَةِ ما أصْحابُ المَشْأمَةِ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 9] — what sort of thing are they?!" This wording follows in Arabic the course of exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub), and from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in addressing His servants it follows the course of that by which a matter is made great in their eyes. Similar to it are ﴿الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 1] ﴿ما الحاقَّةُ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 2] and ﴿القارِعَةُ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 1] ﴿ما القارِعَةُ﴾ [al-Qāriʿa: 2]. The meaning of "أصْحابُ المَيْمَنَةِ" is: the companions of the right hand, and "أصْحابُ المَشْأمَةِ": the companions of the left hand. The companions of the right are the people of the lofty rank, and the companions of the left are the people of the low, base rank.
